inputs.original_text: This looks like a deliberately calibrated strategy: Tom Homan keeps enforcement at polling places on the table, then frames Democrats as “afraid of” something, while the administration preserves room to deny any intent to intimidate. The mixed signals aren’t a harmless muddle—they keep voters uncertain and the threat usable, while responsibility stays conveniently blurred.
inputs.modified_text: This isn’t confusion—it’s the point. Keeping enforcement at polling places on the table while claiming Democrats are “afraid of” something lets the administration pressure voters and still hide behind denials of intent. The ambiguity is a tool: make the threat feel real, keep responsibility blurred, and let officials claim nothing was meant to intimidate anyone.
